newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes down, may head lower later.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes down, may head lower later.

text.p: Gold prices were likely to test lower levels later on Friday after a ruminative morning in Europe, dealers said.
"New York tried to put the price up yesterday (Thursday) but there was no rally and you are left with the impression there is a lot of selling out there," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $351.70 per ounce compared with $353.10 on Thursday afternoon.
Early business was fairly quiet with no real momentum behind the market to move the price from around its fixing level.

New York's lacklustre finish (spot at $351.90/$352.40 and the Comex April futures contract down $0.80 at $353.60) acted as a modest platform for the Far East market, but the firmer yen wiped out most of the gains by the closes in Tokyo and Hong Kong, dealers said.
A lower dollar against the mark was mildly supportive for gold, but attention would be on U.S. payroll and average hourly earnings data for February due at 1330 GMT, dealers said.
Economists forecast the data to show an increase in the U.S. payroll of 230,000 and a 0.4 percent rise in hourly earnings.
"Any positive reaction in the bond market (to the data) could be the final blow for gold," one dealer said.
New York had an "inside" trading day -- when the price range is within the previous day's range -- on Thursday, which did not look positive for Friday, dealers said.
Dealers and analysts forecast a test of support at $350.00.
"The chances are that it will go down rather than up," one said, adding that a breach there could lead to the mid $340s.
That, in turn, could attract renewed producer selling from miners who had set aside sell orders as gold came up from its mid February low of $336 to last week's high of around $363.00.
Technically there was a chance of gold rising to fill a gap on the April Comex chart between $357.70 and $360.10.
But dealers said the market probably lacked the confidence to go for that target.
"The technicals are turning towards further declines," one dealer said.
The market was still shaken following news from Switzerland on Wednesday of a proposal to sell gold from reserves to establish a fund to help victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies.
Silver could dip to $5.12/$5.14 from its 1045 GMT quote of $5.18/$5.20 if gold values fell, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium were unchanged at $380.50/$381.50 and $148.00/$149.00. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
